items.title: Billy Bauer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998
items.q: I looked him up. And him and his wife, Dotty, who he was going — she sent him to Juilliard

ctx.x: Yeah. Everybody came in and sit in with this little trio. Bob Rowe had three strings on his bass. It was a three string bass. To this day I’ve never seen one. And he also played a little guitar, he was sort of a Django Reinhardt type. But anyway, well I didn’t mean to get off, but he had your last name. And he wound up to be the principal bass player in the New Orleans Symphony. Me and my wife went out there when I was on the road, and I looked him up. And him and his wife, Dotty, who he was going — she sent him…
It sounds like a swinging town.
